findings.evidence: `grep -n '^private lemma f4Root_23\|^private lemma f4Coroot_0\|^private lemma f4Root_natAdd' F4.lean` → 443, 447, 367; `grep -n '@\[expose\]' F4.lean` → no hits; module doc lines 17-23 assert the fundamental-weight/simple-coroot bases and the negation convention that no public lemma states.
findings.fix: Make the characteristic value lemmas public: `f4Coroot (Fin.castAdd 44 i) = Pi.single i 1`, `f4Root (Fin.castAdd 44 i) = CartanMatrix.F₄ i`, and `f4Root (Fin.addNat i 24) = -f4Root (Fin.castAdd 44 i)` (same for coroots), as `@[simp]`. Since the point of this datum is that consumers compute with it, also `@[expose]` the two tables (or add per-index value lemmas) so the remaining 44 roots are usable.
findings.issue: `f4Root` (48) and `f4Coroot` (65) are public but their bodies are not `@[expose]`d (the file only opens `public section`, cf. the comment at `DynkinType.lean:228` explaining that `cartanMatrix` needs `@[simp]` value lemmas for exactly this reason), and every value fact about them is `private`: `f4Root_23`/`f4Root_22_add_23`/`f4Root_19_add_20`/`f4Root_20` (443-446), `f4Coroot_0`-`f4Coroot_3` (447-450), `f4Root_natAdd`/`f4Coroot_natAdd` (367, 370), `f4Root_coroot_two` (406). A consumer therefore cannot prove a single coordinate of any of the 48 roots, cannot check that the simple coroots are the standard basis (the `⟨ω_i, α_j^∨⟩ = δ_ij` pinning the roadmap makes an acceptance criterion), and cannot use the documented `root (i+24) = -root i` convention; `decide`/`rfl` fail outside the module.

findings.evidence: Mathlib `Basic.lean:183`: `reflectionPerm i := RootPairing.equiv_of_mapsTo p root coroot i hr hp`; `grep -n 'reflectionPerm' F4.lean` → no hits in the PR file.

findings.issue: `RootPairing.mk'` sets `reflectionPerm i := equiv_of_mapsTo ...`, i.e. `Classical.choose` (Mathlib `LinearAlgebra/RootSystem/Basic.lean:183-189`), so the public datum's Weyl action on root indices is opaque — the exact `Classical.choose` situation Layer 6 exists to avoid. The PR computes the full explicit action (`f4ReflectionTable` 87, `f4ReflectionIndex` 161, `f4ReflectionIndex_root`/`_coroot` 377/391) but keeps it all `private` and never states the identification.

findings.evidence: Line 596-599 LHS is `f4Root (Fin.castAdd 44 i) ⬝ᵥ f4Coroot (Fin.castAdd 44 j)`; lines 617-621 use `simp only [..., f4SimplyConnectedRootDatum_pairing, cartanMatrix_F4]` then `decide`, not the `@[simp]` pinning theorem.
findings.fix: Restate the pinning lemma as `f4SimplyConnectedRootDatum.pairing (f4SimpleIndex i) (f4SimpleIndex j) = CartanMatrix.F₄ i j` with `f4SimpleIndex` (546) made public, or give the four-by-four values at literal indices; make `f4SimplyConnectedBaseEquiv` public so the base's Bourbaki numbering is part of the interface.
findings.issue: `f4SimplyConnectedRootDatum_pairing_eq_cartanMatrix_F4` is stated on the raw tables with `Fin.castAdd 44 i` indices rather than on `f4SimplyConnectedRootDatum.pairing` / `f4SimplyConnectedBase.cartanMatrixIn`, so its `@[simp]` LHS never matches the literal indices `0,1,2,3` a user or the other simp lemma (`f4SimplyConnectedRootDatum_pairing`, 439) produces — the file's own `hasCartanType` proof (615-621) bypasses it and falls back to `decide`. Relatedly, the concrete Bourbaki labelling `f4SimplyConnectedBaseEquiv` (601) is `private`, while `HasCartanType` only asserts an existential relabelling, so no consumer can name which support element is Bourbaki node `i`.

summary: The datum is advertised as explicit but nothing about it is provable downstream: `f4Root`/`f4Coroot` are public with unexposed bodies and no value lemma, every value fact is `private`, and the choice-derived `reflectionPerm` is never linked to the explicit reflection table the PR computes. The Cartan-matrix pinning lemma is also stated in a form that cannot fire.
